title: OTA: Optimal Transport Assignment for Object Detection

problem.summary: Label assignment in dense detectors is usually done independently per ground-truth with fixed or locally dynamic rules, so ambiguous anchors that could belong to several objects are resolved by hand-crafted heuristics; the paper argues this per-object, context-free assignment is sub-optimal and that a global assignment strategy for the one-to-many CNN setting was uncharted.
statements: Classical label assignment matches anchors to ground truth or background with pre-defined rules such as fixed IoU thresholds.
Static division boundaries ignore that appropriate pos/neg boundaries vary with object size, shape and occlusion.
Ambiguous anchors qualified as positive for multiple ground truths are resolved by hand-crafted rules, which can introduce harmful gradients with respect to the other ground truths.
For CNN detectors in one-to-many scenarios, a global optimal assigning strategy remains uncharted.

evidence.quote: Recent advances in label assignment in object detection mainly seek to independently define positive/negative training samples for each ground-truth (gt) object.
However, independently assigning pos/neg samples for each gt without context could be sub-optimal, just like the lack of context may lead to improper prediction.
Such static strategies ignore a fact that for objects with different sizes, shapes or occlusion condition, the appropriate positive/negative (pos/neg) division boundaries may vary.
So far, for the CNN based detectors in one-tomany scenarios, a global optimal assigning strategy remains uncharted.

background.summary: The paper reviews fixed IoU-threshold assignment (Faster R-CNN, RetinaNet), anchor-free center-region assignment (FCOS), and dynamic strategies (FreeAnchor, ATSS, PAA, AutoAssign), plus DETR's global one-to-one Hungarian matching; the gap claimed is global optimal assignment that still works in the one-to-many regime of CNN detectors.

relatedWork.name: Faster R-CNN RPN
relatedWork.quote: Anchor-based detectors usually adopt IoU at a certain threshold as the assigning criterion. For example, RPN in Faster R-CNN [33] uses 0.7 and 0.3 as the positive and negative thresholds, respectively.

relatedWork.name: FCOS
relatedWork.relation: anchor-free center-region assignment treated as positives
relatedWork.quote: Anchor-free detectors like FCOS [38] treat the anchors within the center/bbox region of any gt object as the corresponding positives.

relatedWork.name: ATSS
relatedWork.relation: dynamic assignment baseline OTA is compared against
relatedWork.quote: ATSS [47] proposes an adaptive sample selection strategy that adopts mean+std of IoU values from a set of closest anchors for each gt as a pos/neg threshold.

relatedWork.name: DETR
relatedWork.relation: prior global-view assignment, but restricted to one-to-one matching
relatedWork.quote: DeTR [3] is the first work that attempts to consider label assignment from global view. It replaces the detection head with transformer layers [39] and considers one-to-one assignment using the Hungarian algorithm that matches only one query for each gt with global minimum loss.

evidence.quote: These methods explore the optimal assigning strategy for individual objects, while failing to consider context information from a global perspective.
existing assignment strategies are heavily based on hand-crafted rules (e.g., Min Area [38], Max IoU [16, 21, 47].)

solution.summary: OTA casts label assignment as an Optimal Transport problem in which each ground truth is a supplier of k positive labels, each anchor (across all FPN levels) a demander of one label, and background a supplier of the remaining negative labels, with transport costs built from pairwise classification and regression losses; the plan is solved by Sinkhorn-Knopp iteration, refined with a Center Prior and a Dynamic k Estimation of each ground truth's label supply.
solution.approach: Solve a global linear-programming assignment (min total pairwise cls+reg transport cost with supply/demand constraints) via entropic-regularised Sinkhorn-Knopp iteration instead of per-ground-truth hand-crafted rules.
components: Cost matrix of pairwise classification and regression losses between every anchor-gt pair
Background supplier that covers all remaining (negative) labels
Sinkhorn-Knopp iteration solving the regularised OT problem (gamma=0.1, T=50)
Center Prior: only the r^2 closest anchors per FPN level are low-cost candidates
Dynamic k Estimation: sum of the top-q IoU values sets each gt's number of positive labels
IoU branch auxiliary head borrowed from YOLOv1/PAA

evidence.quote: To achieve the global optimal assigning result under the one-to-many situation, we propose to formulate label assignment as an Optimal Transport (OT) problem - a special form of Linear Programming (LP) in Optimization Theory.
we define each gt as a supplier who supplies a certain number of labels, and define each anchor as a demander who needs one unit label.

After formulation, finding the best assignment solution is converted to solve the optimal transport plan, which can be quickly and efficiently solved by the off-the-shelf Sinkhorn-Knopp Iteration [5]. We name such an assigning strategy as Optimal Transport Assignment (OTA).
we propose a simple but effective method to roughly estimate the appropriate number of positive anchors for each gt based on the IoU values between predicted bounding boxes and gts.

experiments.summary: Experiments run on MS COCO 2017 (ablations on val, comparisons on test-dev) with FCOS- and RetinaNet-based detectors using ResNet/ResNeXt-FPN backbones under 1x/180k schedules, plus CrowdHuman validation for crowded pedestrian detection; ablations cover Center Prior, IoU branch, Dynamic k, the radius r and ambiguity handling.

evidence.quote: a single FCOS-ResNet-50 detector equipped with Optimal Transport Assignment (OTA) can reach 40.7% mAP under 1× scheduler, outperforming all other existing assigning methods.
our method with ResNet-101-FPN achieves 45.3% AP, outperforms all other methods with the same backbone including ATSS (43.6% AP), AutoAssign (44.5% AP) and PAA (44.6% AP).
our OTA takes a step forward by introducing global information into the label assignment, boosting MR to 46.6%.
Results in Table 4 shows that dynamic k surpasses the best performance of fixed k by 0.4% AP, validating our point and the effectiveness of Dynamic k Estimation strategy.

limitations.summary: The paper has no dedicated limitations section, but it acknowledges that OTA still relies on a Center Prior for stability, that its one-to-one (k=1) form performs poorly under the 1x schedule, that assignment is sensitive to the candidate radius r, and that training time increases by up to 20%.
items: A hand-crafted Center Prior is still needed to stabilize training despite the global optimization formulation.
With k=1 (one-to-one assignment) OTA performs poorly under the 1x scheduler without auxiliary one-to-many supervision.
The candidate radius r controls accuracy: performance drops when r grows (ATSS 39.4 to 37.2, OTA 40.7 to 40.4 for r=3 to 7).
OTA increases total training time by less than 20% (matrix multiplications run on GPU).

evidence.quote: for general detection datasets like COCO, we find the Center Prior still benefit the training of OTA.

When k=1, OTA becomes a one-to-one assigning strategy, the same as in DeTR. The poor performance tells us that achieving competitive performance via one-to-one assignment under the 1× scheduler remains challenging

equations.name: optimal transport objective
equations.expr: min_pi sum_i sum_j c_ij * pi_ij subject to row/column supply and demand constraints

equations.name: foreground transport cost
equations.expr: c_fg_ij = L_cls(P_cls_j, G_cls_i) + alpha * L_reg(P_box_j, G_box_i)

equations.name: supply vector
equations.expr: s_i = k for i <= m, s_(m+1) = n - m*k

equations.name: entropic regularised OT
equations.expr: min_pi sum_ij (c_ij * pi_ij + gamma * pi_ij * (log pi_ij - 1))

applications.detail: OTA is evaluated on the CrowdHuman benchmark (about 22.6 persons per image) and reports state-of-the-art one-stage results in crowd scenarios, where ambiguous anchors are frequent.
applications.quote: CrowdHuman contains 15000, 4370, and 5000 images in training, validation, and test set, respectively, with the average number of persons in an image 22.6.

applications.detail: One-stage detectors lag two-stage detectors on CrowdHuman; OTA closes and reverses that gap via global assignment.
applications.quote: RetinaNet and FCOS only achieve 58.8% and 55.0% MR respectively, which are far worse than two stage detectors like Faster R-CNN (with FPN), revealing the dilemma of one-stage detectors in crowd scenarios.

deploymentClaims: OTA only adds under 20% to total training time and adds no cost at testing time.
The OT solve is matrix multiplications that can be accelerated on GPUs.

evidence.quote: OTA only increases the total training time by less than 20% and is totally cost-free in testing phase.
